newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

ISRAEL, Oct 1 - Haifa - Five vessels due 1-2 days delay. Expected delays for loading/discharging at berth general cargo up to 5 days, bulk up to 3 days, containers 2 days, tankers, passenger 1 day. Delays at anchorage to load/discharge general cargo up to 1 day, bulk up to 2 days. 1 vessel bunkering 5 vessels under repairs 4 awaiting orders. Ashdod - one to 2 days delay expected. Delays for loading/discharging at berth general cargo up to 9 days, bulk 2-4 days, containers 2 days. Delays for waiting at anchorage to load/discharge general cargo 1 day, bulk up to 1 day, containers 1 day. Eilat delays to loading/discharging at berth bulk 1 day, passenger 1 day.
JORDAN, Sept 28 - Aqaba no vessels due, 4 vessels loading at berth, 9 discharging at berth, 1 at anchorage, 4 waiting at anchorage to load, 3 to discharge, 2 awaiting orders.

MAURITIUS, Oct 1 - Port Louis port working normally. All berths occupied, 2 container vessels and 3 general cargo vessels discharging and loading, 1 vessel loading bulk sugar. Approx. 70 foreign vessels in port. Port labour normal.

MOZAMBIQUE, Sept 30 - Nacala - port working normally (first come, first served basis). No restriction on berthing and sailing at night subject to gratuity to pilot. Draft restriction 9.5 metres plus height of tide at general cargo berths, 14 metres at container. One tug. Beira - general cargo berths working normally (first come, first served). Container/other terminals working normally. Pilotage only in daylight, two tugs operational. Night navigation by special arrangement, restricted to LOA 130 metres. Maputo pilotage only in daylight. Two tugs, one out of order. All berths working normally and expected to remain so (first come, first served). Draft restriction in channel 9 metres less 0.5 metre plus rise of tide.
NAMIBIA, Walvis Bay - Sept 30 - working normally.

SIERRA LEONE, Sept 30 - Freetown - Three vessels due of which 2 container dischargers, 1 container loader. No delays expected. Vessels discharging/loading at berth 1 mill feed loader, 2 rice dischargers, 1 container discharger, 1 aid cargo loader. Vessels anchored. 1 rice discharger. Vessels must be in/out of port before 1900 hours.

SOUTH AFRICA, Sept 30 - Richards Bay - general cargo berths fully committed. Bulk import berths delays of 20-30 days. Bulk export working normally. Bulk coal berths 4 vessels alongside. 8 Anchored. 15 due during next 7 days. 2-3 days berthing delay, expected to continue for rest of week. Durban - Container terminal delays of up to 36 hours. Point/New Pier/Maydon wharf berths working normally. Maize terminal (maydon wharf 8) 5 maize loaders for October. Citrus terminal tapering off as season is closing mid-October. Bunker supplies tight, delays expected due to bunching. Drydock and floating dock 95% booked for October. Bunker barge Durban servicer out of commission 11-14/10 inclusive for repairs/surveys. No replacement arranged yet. East London - general cargo/combi terminal berths extremely busy but no delays expected. Drydock fully booked for October. Copper moving in small parcels of 2,500 tonnes per month in containers to Far East. Elevator 1 vessel on load berth and another due on 10/10. No delays. Gasoil pipeline under-utilised. Log loaders 15,000 cubic metres on hand. Scrap steel 8,000 tonnes on hand for shipment mid-Oct. Wheat 1 vessel due on 11/10 and one on 15/10. Tankers - one in port. Port Elizabeth working normally. 3 vessels in port. No delays on general, ore, tanker, fruit or container berths. 2 citrus vessels due. Cape Town breakbulk no delays, vessels working on arrival. Container terminal no delays. 2 new gantry cranes fully operational. Bunker berths no delays. Drydock and repair quay fully occupied, booking essential. Saldanha Bay working normally.

TUNISIA, Sept 28 - Gabes - Two tankers loading at berth. 2 vessels discharging at berth (1 bulk flour, 1 bulk sulphur). Sfax - one vessel loading bulk salt. Tunis - one vessel awaiting instructions, 1 general cargo, 1 motor tanker loading olive oil. Rades - three ro/ro vessels in port. Goulette - north side 1 discharging bulk maize, 1eneral cargo, 1 passenger vessel, 1 military. South side 1 vessel discharging grain. Two vessels in roads. Sousse - no vessels in port. No waiting time.

TURKEY, Oct 1 - Istanbul, Haydarpasa - 9 vessels operating of which 4 containers, 4 dry cargo, 1 ro/ro. No berthing delays, except for heavy lift cargoes. Galata - 9 cargo/passenger vessels operating. Port congested. Ambarli - 3 operating. No berthing delays. Mersin - 19 operating of which loading 2 cement, 1 tobacco, 1 general cargo, 2 citrus, 1 chrome ore, 1 legumes. Discharging - 1 iron, 1 sodium phosphate, 1 corn oil. Loading/discharging - 1 vehicle/general cargo, 1 vehicle, 3 container vessels. Free zone piers - 1 vessel loading chrome, 1 loading rice, 1 discharging sugar. Seka - no vessels in port.

UAE, Sept 29 - Dubai - vessels operating in port 22/9-28/9 83 container, 1 general cargo, 6 general cargo/container, 2 bulkers, 4 car carriers, 1 livestock carrier, 13 tankers, 4 naval, 6 UAE naval, 1 bunkers/repairs/stores, 6 dhows, 11 barges, 8 tugs, 1 lpg tanker, 20 supply, 2 ngl tankers, 1 vlcc. No waiting time. Vessels due 30 containers, 10 general cargo, 6 tankers. No delays. Discharging at berth 2 containers, 3 general, 3 tankers. Under repairs/drydock 6 general, 10 tankers.

YEMEN, Sept 30 - Hodeidah - all berths occupied except No.1. Vessels alongside 1 bulk wheat, 1 wheatflour, 1 steel, 1 general cargo, 2 containers. Anchored 2 bulk corn/rice, 1 bulk wheat, 1 container. Waiting time general cargo up to 2 days, bagged up to 4 days, bulk up to 6 days, containers up to 1 day. Mokha - one vessel discharging wheatflour alongside, no vessels anchored, no delays. Oct 1 - Hodeidah - vessels berthed 1 flour, 2 bulk wheat, 1 general cargo, 1 soybeans, 1 soy/corn. No vessels awaiting berth. Delays reefers/general cargo (steel, timber, powder) 24 hours, bagged cargo (sugar, rice, flour) 2-3 Days. Bulk wheat/corn 7-10 days, no delays for container vessels.
